questions.q: What framework are Sentinel workbooks actually built on?
options: Azure Workbooks, an Azure Monitor reporting framework reused across many Azure services
A reporting engine written specifically and exclusively for Sentinel
Power BI, embedded directly inside the Sentinel blade
A third-party visualization add-on installed separately from Sentinel
questions.explain: Sentinel's Workbooks page surfaces the same Azure Workbooks framework used elsewhere in Azure Monitor, pre-pointed at Sentinel's data.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the building-block steps a workbook is assembled from?
options: A stored procedure step
A text step
A query step
A parameter step
questions.explain: Workbooks are built from text, query, parameter, and link steps — there is no stored procedure step; that's a SQL Server concept, not a KQL/workbook one.

questions.q: What is a workbook's query step actually backed by?
options: A real KQL query run against the Log Analytics workspace
A static image uploaded by the workbook's author
A pre-aggregated export file refreshed once a day
A separate database outside of Sentinel entirely
questions.explain: Every chart or table in a workbook is the live output of a KQL query run against the same Log Analytics workspace covered in Lesson 2.

questions.q: What does a parameter step let a reader of a workbook do?
options: Change an input, like a time range or hostname, and have other steps re-run live against the new value
Edit the underlying KQL query's syntax directly on the canvas
Export the workbook to a PDF automatically every night
Grant other analysts permission to view the workbook
questions.explain: A parameter step is a control — a dropdown or time-range picker — that other steps are wired to, so changing it re-runs those steps against the new value.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a workbook is more useful than a static dashboard screenshot during an investigation?
options: Because an analyst can reshape it live by changing a parameter, instead of being stuck with the view the author first built
Because workbooks load faster than any other Azure feature
Because workbooks don't require a Log Analytics workspace at all
Because static dashboards are being fully removed from Sentinel
questions.explain: A screenshot freezes one moment; a workbook lets the reader narrow a time range or filter to one account and see the same queries re-run immediately.
